note: RoboARC (RoboARC on MuJoCo, docs/benchmarks/roboarc.md): written by scripts/robotangle/release_rebuild.py --onto on dev/robotangle_mujoco. release_commit: the dev/robotangle_mujoco commit the image, the tooling and the instances come from; runtime: the image's installed runtime; bases: one record per task base (ported_from / template, instance, facts the texts state, evidence). Until the first release this holds the shared fields of RoboARC's release.json and no base.
runtime_notes: source = the public simulator source of release_commit (images/topogym/prune.py rule); python, dependencies: the release's pinned locks; uipc_build_sha256 = the audited libuipc wheel of every lab evidence image (merged-v17..v19), installed with UIPC_WHEEL=prebuilt (images/roboarc/README.md); it is the image's default build (/opt/uipc-build.json). uipc_builds: the two libuipc builds of one recipe (same pyuipc version and source commit, which the frozen IPC settled states hold) that the tooling chooses from at Session start, before uipc is imported (rcb_topogym.select_uipc_build): the audited wheel on compute capability 8.9 and 12.x or without a visible GPU, the sm86 build (/opt/uipc_sm86) on any other GPU. A task's runtime binding carries both (uipc_builds); the session's runtime_binding names the one in use.

audited.rule: compute capability 8.9 or 12.x (SASS sm_89, sm_120), or no visible GPU

sm86.rule: any other compute capability: SASS sm_86 on 8.6 and 8.7, its compute_86 PTX (driver JIT) on 9.x and 10.x

buzz-wire-3d-01-i01.grasp_rules: assisted grasping (contact_weld_v1): a gripper whose command moves towards closed takes hold of a graspable part (wand) once both fingers touch the same part inside its grasp region, the tool frame within 6 cm of it and the penetration at most 2 mm, for 0.02 s; the part then follows the gripper rigidly. Any command that opens the gripper (by more than 0.2 % of its travel) lets it go. A hold that breaks (the fingers open more than 15 %, the part drifts 1 cm / 0.15 rad from its held pose, the hold has to push or pull its part with more than 65 N averaged over 20 ms, or no finger has touched the part for 0.2 s) is lost, and the gripper must open before it can take hold again; that force is reached when, for example, two held parts that hook into each other are pulled apart, or a held part is pressed into another object. Two grippers never hold the same part; other objects are grasped physically (friction)
